sections.h2: Rice and wheat carry the MSP guarantee; no other crop passes 15% of its harvest

chart.title: Only rice (36.3%) and wheat (22.6%) pass 15% of their harvest
chart.sub: Share of the harvest reached by procurement at MSP, %.
chart.source: Procurement series cited in the post.

sections.means: Rice and wheat are the only crops where the MSP promise has a standing buyer, so the other MSP crops are largely promises without a purchaser.
sections.todo: Publish a per-crop volume ratio before sowing for the crops with no standing procurement, starting with the grain book's buy rows.

sections.h2: Rice and wheat procurement swings least; tur, bajra and maize swing most

chart.title: Rice and wheat vary 21-24% a year; tur, bajra and maize vary 109-120%
chart.sub: Year-to-year coefficient of variation of procured volume, %.
chart.source: Procurement series cited in the post.

sections.means: A purchase guarantee whose volume swings by more than 100% a year gives a farmer no reliable basis for choosing what to sow.
sections.todo: Announce each crop's purchase volume before sowing, so that the guarantee holds in a bad year as well as a good one.

sections.h2: Tur imports land 29% below its MSP, so tur buying needs duty coordination

chart.title: Tur imports land at ₹5,659 a quintal, below its ₹8,000 MSP
chart.sub: Tur MSP against FY26 CIF import price, ₹ per quintal.
chart.source: DGCI&S; MSP as cited in the post.

sections.means: Duty-free imports at ₹5,659 undercut the ₹8,000 MSP, so any domestic tur buffer would compete directly with cheaper imports.
sections.todo: Set tariff policy alongside any tur volume guarantee before the first quintal is bought.
